note: v1 89.17 (seeds 0/11 89.17/89.19), first draft of MATH-ROCK INTERPLAY, 'Floor 31': an office tower at night with every light left on, the building's machinery as music, ~7:05 in six movements at 132 bpm. A seven-note tapped FIGURE (D-F-A-C-A-F-E) is re-cut by every meter it passes through - 5/4 lobby, 7/8 interlock, 6/8 stairwell, 5/4 atrium, 7/8 machine squaring into 4/4, 4/4 roof - and a second guitar plays 4/4 phrases against the first's 7/8, the two realigning only every seven bars (compscore's polymeter: 100). The lift is the speech: a chime and an announcement voice calling floors between phrases ('going up, floor thirty one', 'doors closing', and at the very end, far below the roof, 'ground floor'); a clock ticks in the quiet movements. The machine brings two chug rigs on the 2+2+3, and the roof resolves to F major with the e-bow and wind. Levels 100 (-16.6 LUFS, dynamic, TP -2.1).

v2 89.69 (seeds 0/11 89.69/90.10 vs v1 89.17/89.19): A FLOOR UNDER IT - Harry's 'strong bass' note carried into the new album, done as body rather than boom. The sub's lowest tones (32-52 Hz) were booming 10 dB over the genre while the body of the guitars, the picked bass and the chug rigs (100-210 Hz) sat 6-9 dB under it, so the interlock had rumble but no weight. The master now trims the boom (a 34 Hz high-pass, -4 dB at 45 Hz, the sub 2 dB down) and lifts the body (+5 dB at 115 Hz, +3 at 170 Hz), with the top a touch darker (-3 dB at 4.2 kHz). Spectrum 88 -> 93; levels 100 (-16.6 LUFS, dynamic).

v3 92.93 (seeds 0/11 92.93/93.39, level with v2 re-scored under the album's new measures 92.97/93.44): THE OFFICE AT NIGHT - Harry's 'synth'd sound effects', put to work in the meter. In the Machine's opening sixteen bars (drums and bass alone) and the Atrium's second half, a photocopier scans on every bar - its sweep lands on each 7/8 (and 5/4) downbeat, so the building's machinery literally keeps the odd meter before the guitars take it over; and in the Stairwell, between the celesta's figure and the clock, a phone rings three times far down a corridor and nobody answers. The lift's voice now has a building around it.

v4 92.86 (seeds 0/11 92.86/92.94, level with v3 92.93/93.39): THE GUITARS AGREE - the piece's payoff. For six movements the two guitars disagree about where the bar is (the tapped FIGURE re-cut by 5/4, 7/8 and 6/8 while the second guitar keeps its own 4/4 phrases, meeting only every seven bars). Now, on the roof, after the climb resolves to F major, THE FIGURE is played for sixteen bars in octave unison on one clean guitar voice brought forward into the echo and the hall, on the same 4/4 bar - the two lines finally meet, and the e-bow and the wind take it from there. Measured about 9-10 dB under the full roof mix: a lead moment, not a background line. (Raising the sub an octave for body cost spectrum 93 -> 89 and was reverted.)
